question: Within 15 minutes, does NQ reach an upper barrier first, an equal lower barrier first, or neither - and do NQ's own context or the intermarket inputs predict it better than training frequencies?
barrier: +-1.0 x fan_rw_v2's walk-forward sigma of the log price to 15 minutes (known at issuance), around the log of the origin's last close
path: the active contract's 1-minute TRADES bars starting in the 15 minutes after the origin; the first minute whose high >= the upper or whose low <= the lower barrier decides; both in that minute = ambiguous; none = neither. Origins as the fan scores them (a price at both ends inside the trading day)
ambiguous: left out of training and selection; evaluated under both assignments (up first, down first); their share reported. No finer data is stored

predictors.A: freq: the block's training class frequencies
predictors.B: own: HistGradientBoostingClassifier on NQ ret1/ret5/ret15, vwap_dist, rv15, rv60, vol60, phase (categorical)
predictors.C: intermarket: B's inputs plus fan_im_dir_v1's intermarket set (14)

selection: lowest mean session multiclass Brier on the validation sessions (the last 20% of training, models fitted on the sessions before them); refitted on every training session. No activation interval: A is itself a fitted forecast and the out-of-sample blocks decide

evaluation.blocks: fan_intermarket_v2's three checks and its spent holdout in two blocks of 30 (150 sessions, all development)
evaluation.score: multiclass Brier, sum over the three classes of (p - outcome)^2, session means
evaluation.calibration: reliability per class in deciles, non-ambiguous origins

hypotheses.H1: B beats A: NQ's own context predicts first hits
hypotheses.H2: C beats B and A: the intermarket inputs add (beating B alone could reflect B overfitting)

decision.pass: the hypothesis's differences (H1: B - A; H2: C - B and C - A) have their 97.5% session-level intervals wholly below zero under both ambiguity assignments (Bonferroni over H1 and H2)
decision.fail: a mean difference is not below zero under either assignment
decision.directional: a passing model counts as directional only if it also beats its symmetric version (P(up) and P(down) averaged) with the 95 % interval wholly below zero under both assignments; otherwise its information is about whether a barrier is reached, i.e. size
decision.after_pass: freeze, then fresh forward data before any probabilities are shown

display: none: kept apart from the fan
